transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-14 15:30 PST | Duration: ~42 min | Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Zenwell CTO), Sara Li (Zenwell Head of ML), Ben Ortiz (Zenwell SRE)

Summary: Quick demo focused on rate limiting, quotas and multi-tenant controls (org/project keys) in the Redwood Console and API. Covered per-project quotas, burst behavior, reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) and security controls. Agreed next steps: send rate-limit template and SOC 2/security deck, run a POC benchmark next week.

Topics: Rate limiting model (tokens/minute, requests/sec), org vs project level quotas, API keys & project keys, console UI for whitelisting and throttling, integration with billing and alerts, Dedicated fallback and routing policies, RBAC and audit logs.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy valentine's day. I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Michael Torres: Doing well thanks, short on time so appreciate the focus. We want to make sure we can isolate teams, set quotas per product line and not blow the budget if something spikes.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Great, we'll demo the console and API flows. We'll show org-level caps, project keys for teams, and how rate limits surface in logs and alerts. We'll also touch on Dedicated options for reserved capacity.
[00:30] Sara Li: Important for us is per-team token budgets and ensuring our dev/test keys can't use prod quota. Also SSO is a hard requirement.
[00:40] Ben Ortiz: And does the rate limiting play well with KV cache and streaming? We do a lot of chat streams.
[00:48] Priya Shah: Good question. There are separate controls for streaming requests; the service counts tokens similarly but you can set concurrent connection caps and per-key QPS. We'll show where that is.

[01:15] Alex Kim: Quick agenda: 1) Console walkthrough for org/project keys and quota config, 2) API examples for rate-limited responses and headers, 3) monitoring + alerts, 4) licensing/POC next steps.

[02:05] Priya Shah: Jumping into the Console — note, some product names in the UI are slightly different in the export, sometimes shows Redwood-UI v2 — ignore that, it's our internal lab. Here, you can see the org settings, there's an Org Quotas tab. You can set overall token budget per month and a safety buffer.
[02:35] Priya Shah: Creating a project key: Project > Create key > assign to team; keys are scoped to projects and you can pin model versions and quota policies to a key. This is useful so dev keys can't accidentally call high-cost models.
[03:05] Michael Torres: Can we set different token budgets per project and also set a global org cap?
[03:12] Priya Shah: Yes, global org cap acts as a hard ceiling. Individual project quotas are enforced first; if a project reaches its quota, requests are rejected with HTTP 429 and a specific error that indicates "quota_exceeded".
[03:25] Alex Kim: We also support soft limits where we can throttle down to reduced throughput before cutting off, so apps can degrade gracefully.

[04:00] Ben Ortiz: What about bursts — if a team has sudden traffic, can we allow temporary bursts?
[04:06] Priya Shah: There's a burst allowance and token bucket implementation — you can configure burst windows and burst capacity per project; also an emergency override for org admins if needed. However burst usage counts towards the monthly budget.

[05:00] Priya Shah: API behavior — when you hit a rate limit we return 429 with headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. For token quotas we include X-Quota-Used and X-Quota-Remaining with human-readable messages in the body. (Note: header names may differ slightly in started doc, sometimes shows X-RLimit.)
[05:45] Sara Li: Are headers present for streaming responses too?
[05:49] Priya Shah: For streaming we send initial headers but you get periodic control frames; the client can subscribe to quota events. There's also a webhook for quota alerts.

[06:30] Alex Kim: On billing integration: project keys are tied to billable units and invoices can be broken down by project. That helps with showback and chargebacks.

[07:10] Priya Shah: Switching to policies: You can set rate limit policies per model family, e.g., smaller models get higher QPS but lower token cap; large models like high-context LLMs may have stricter per-token limits. We have presets for common patterns.
[07:45] Michael Torres: For our regulated workloads, we might want Private deployment. How do quotas work in Redwood Private / Dedicated?
[07:54] Alex Kim: In Dedicated or Private you still use the same control plane for quotas; for fully air-gapped on-prem you can run the control plane locally or we can ship a management bundle. Quotas are enforced at the edge nodes; and audit logs are kept in your KMS/stack.
[08:20] Ben Ortiz: KMS integration — we use AWS KMS.
[08:24] Priya Shah: We support AWS KMS and customer HSMs; keys are stored per org and you can rotate them. Audit entries show key use per request.

[09:00] Priya Shah: Quick demo of an example: I’ll use curl to show hitting a project key that has a 1M tokens/month quota and 1000 tokens/minute.
[09:10] [screen share noises]
[09:20] Priya Shah: (typing) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_key_abc123" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":512}'
[09:35] Priya Shah: Response shows a 200 with X-Quota-Remaining in header. If I bump the token usage above the per-minute cap you’ll see 429 with quota_exceeded.
[10:05] Alex Kim: Note — we sometimes see customers confuse request rate with token rate; both matter. For chat it's common to hit token limits faster due to long contexts.

[10:40] Sara Li: Can we set retention rules for logs/audit? We have retention policies at 7 years for some logs.
[10:48] Priya Shah: We have configurable retention in the Console; longer retention is an add-on. For Private you can keep everything in your own storage to meet regulatory retention.

[11:30] Priya Shah: Alerts — you can set thresholds (e.g., 80% of project quota) and choose alert channels: email, webhook, Slack. There's built-in suppression to avoid alert floods.
[11:55] Ben Ortiz: Will alerts contain sample request ids so we can trace back fast?
[12:00] Priya Shah: Yes, alerts include sample request ids and links to the trace in the Console.

[12:30] Alex Kim: On the topic of multi-tenant controls, we also support org-level policies like disallowed models and allowed endpoints per project. You can block higher-cost models for dev projects.

[13:05] Michael Torres: What happens when we roll out a new team — is there an onboarding flow?
[13:10] Priya Shah: You can create template policies for projects, and there's an API to programmatically create project keys and assign quotas, so provisioning can be automated.

[13:45] Priya Shah: Demoing the API docs: here's the /v1/keys endpoint. You can POST to create a key with fields: project_id, scopes, quota_policy_id. The response returns the key string once — we encourage storing it in your secret store. (Note: older doc versions said /keys/create.)

[14:30] Sara Li: We want to run a POC with 10k QPS style workload to validate tail latency and throttling behavior. How do we run a bench?
[14:38] Priya Shah: For benchmarks we'll provide a sample workload harness (k6 script + small Python runner). We'll run it against a dedicated test project. For heavy loads we recommend Redwood Dedicated where you get reserved capacity and predictable latency.

[15:10] Alex Kim: Could mention Redwood Optimize — it will recommend batching, quantization profiles, and suggest model variants to hit cost/latency targets. It can also recommend quota configurations based on historical usage.

[16:00] Michael Torres: Security questions: SOC 2, SAML, RBAC, audit logs — can you send the security deck?
[16:06] Alex Kim: Yes, we'll send SOC 2 and our security pack; dashboard supports SAML SSO and granular RBAC for project-level admin roles.

[16:40] Priya Shah: Back to throttling: We support graceful degradation policies — e.g., automatically fallback to a smaller model or serve cached responses when the quota is near exhaustion. That is configurable in the routing policies.

[17:20] Ben Ortiz: If a rogue job uses up a project's tokens, is there an emergency kill switch?
[17:25] Priya Shah: Org admins can pause keys and revoke them instantly from the Console; there's also an API to rotate/revoke keys. We recommend pairing with alerts and automated playbooks.

[18:05] Michael Torres: How are per-minute limits enforced across regions? We're multi-region (NA/EU).
[18:12] Alex Kim: Limits are enforced per org globally but there are region-aware routing policies; you can set region-specific quotas if you need residency controls. For example EU projects can have separate quotas and billing.

[19:00] Priya Shah: Showing the audit logs — each request shows project_id, key_id (redacted in UI), model_used, tokens_consumed, timestamp and outcome. You can export logs to S3 or BigQuery.

[20:10] Sara Li: Any gotchas around streaming and retries?
[20:15] Priya Shah: Retries should respect idempotency; for streaming we suggest client-side backoffs and using the provided retry headers. If you retry the same prompt, prefix cache may reduce cost.

[21:00] Alex Kim: Pricing note — quotas align with billing tiers; overage protection can be strict or loose depending on your billing agreement. For Dedicated we do committed spend.

[21:30] Michael Torres: Ok we want to move to a short POC — what's the minimum data you need?
[21:36] Priya Shah: We'll need list of models you plan to use, a sample workload and a test project we can provision, plus SRE contact for any network setup. We'll run baseline and peak tests and share results.

[22:10] Priya Shah: I'll demo a throttling scenario: artificially hit the per-minute token cap to show the 429 response and Console metrics blinking red.
[22:20] [typing/demo sounds] \n[22:40] Priya Shah: Here's the 429 body: {"error":"quota_exceeded","message":"Project quota exceeded: project_monthly_tokens"} — sometimes transcription shows different keys.

[23:20] Ben Ortiz: Useful. Can we get a CSV export of per-project usage for our finance team?
[23:25] Priya Shah: Yes, usage export is available with daily granularity and project breakdown.

[24:10] Alex Kim: Recap: org cap + project quotas, project keys, burst windows, streaming controls, alerts, Dedicated for reserved capacity, and Optimize recommendations.

[24:35] Michael Torres: Any concerns about vendor lock-in with routing/fallback features?
[24:40] Alex Kim: We design the API to be consistent; fallback policies are model-agnostic. If you need on-prem, Private gives more control. We also provide exportable configs and infra-as-code templates.

[25:20] Priya Shah: Showed where to create quota policy templates and assign them to projects; also demoed automated onboarding via API.

[26:00] Sara Li: For the POC, can Redwood simulate a team hitting 80% quota and show degradation path?
[26:06] Priya Shah: Yes, we can run staged load test with an orchestrated increase and show the fallback rules. We'll record graphs and share.

[27:00] Michael Torres: On legal/procurement, do you have standard BAA or HIPAA addendum?
[27:06] Alex Kim: We have HIPAA-ready Private deployments and a BAA is available for customers on enterprise plans — we'll loop in sales/legal.

[28:10] Ben Ortiz: Are there any rate-limit headers we should code against that might change?
[28:15] Priya Shah: We keep the headers stable for major versions; if we change we'll version the API and deprecate headers with notice. Also we provide SDKs that surface the headers as structured fields.

[29:00] Alex Kim: Quick note — sometimes in our older docs the KV cache is referenced as K-V cache or KC cache; apologies for typos in auto-export.

[29:20] Michael Torres: That's fine. Can you send the demo recording and a short runbook for our SREs?
[29:25] Alex Kim: Yes, we'll send the recording and a runbook + rate-limit template.

[30:00] Priya Shah: Live Q/A — Sara: will we be able to pin model versions per project?
[30:05] Priya Shah: Yes, you can pin exact model hashes or use a model alias pinned to a semantic version. If you want automatic rollouts we support canary policies.

[31:00] Sara Li: And alerts can integrate with PagerDuty?
[31:05] Priya Shah: Yep, webhooks, PagerDuty, Slack.

[31:40] Michael Torres: Timeline: we want POC next week and decide by end of month. Is that doable?
[31:46] Alex Kim: Totally. Priya, can you own the POC?
[31:50] Priya Shah: Yep, I'll run the benchmark and be primary SE.

[32:05] Action review (verbal): Alex to send pricing and security docs; Priya to share test harness; Michael to provide access and sample workload.

[33:00] Priya Shah: One more demo note — Optimize can suggest moving some traffic to a quantized variant to save token spend while meeting quality SLOs. We can include Optimize recommendations in the POC report.

[34:10] Michael Torres: For billing separation, is it per-project invoice or combined invoice with breakdown?
[34:15] Alex Kim: Combined invoice with line-item breakdown per project; for enterprise we can do separate billing arrangements.

[35:00] Sara Li: Any SLA around rate limit enforcement or latency?
[35:05] Alex Kim: For hosted API we publish latency SLOs; for Dedicated we have SLA-backed latency/uptime commitments. We'll include that in the docs.

[36:10] Ben Ortiz: One more: would we be able to auto-rotate project keys via API?
[36:15] Priya Shah: Yes, rotate/revoke endpoints available. We recommend rotating keys regularly and can integrate with your secret manager.

[37:00] Alex Kim: Wrap-up — Priya will send the POC plan and schedule the first run. Alex will send pricing and security pack. Michael will follow up with access and timeline.

[38:00] Michael Torres: Thanks, that was useful.

[38:05] Sara Li: Appreciate the clarity.

[38:10] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with all artifacts.

[41:30] End of recording.

References & shared artifacts: "Rate-limit config template" (link shared in chat), SOC 2 & security deck (link to packet), POC harness (k6 + Python runner link), demo recording link (will be shared).

Notes on transcription: Auto-generated; occasional product name typos (Redwood-UI v2, K-V cache) and header names may differ.

Next steps (recap): 1) Alex send security + pricing + demo recording (by 2026-02-17); 2) Priya share test harness and run POC (by 2026-02-18); 3) Michael provision test access and sample workload (by 2026-02-20).
